programs.name: HELP Grant (Higher Education Legislative Plan)
programs.summary: Full tuition at Mississippi public colleges for students with a 2.5 GPA, a 20 ACT, the HELP high school courses, and a Pell Grant from the FAFSA.

also: The HELP high school course list
A full or partial Pell Grant from the FAFSA
Family income under the HELP limit
MAAPP by March 31 of senior year

award.summary: Full tuition and required fees at Mississippi public colleges for up to 8 semesters (private colleges: the average public amount).

programs.name: Mississippi Eminent Scholars Grant (MESG)
programs.summary: For a 3.5 GPA and a 29 ACT (1350 SAT), or National Merit semifinalists and finalists.

award.summary: Up to $2,500 a year (not more than tuition).

programs.name: Mississippi Tuition Assistance Grant (MTAG)
programs.summary: For a 2.5 GPA and a 15 ACT. Not for students who get the largest Pell Grant.

also: Not eligible with the maximum Pell Grant

award.summary: Up to $500 a year as a freshman and sophomore and $1,000 a year as a junior and senior.

programs.name: Nissan Scholarship
programs.summary: Full tuition, fees and books at a Mississippi public college for seniors with a 2.5 GPA, a 20 ACT, financial need and leadership. Separate application and essay.

also: Apply by March 1 of senior year

award.summary: Full tuition, required fees and a book allowance for up to four years.

aid_steps.title: Mississippi Aid Application (MAAPP)
aid_steps.summary: Mississippi's state grants (HELP, MTAG and MESG) need their own state application, the MAAPP, besides the FAFSA.
how: Create an account on the Mississippi Office of Student Financial Aid site and complete the MAAPP after October 1 of senior year.
For HELP, submit by March 31 and send the documents it asks for by April 30.
For MTAG and MESG, the deadline is September 15, but there's no reason to wait.
watch_out: The state says these deadlines are set by law, with no exceptions.

counselor_notes: Mississippi's state aid needs the MAAPP state application: HELP (full tuition; 2.5 GPA, 20 ACT, HELP courses and a Pell Grant; due March 31), MESG (3.5 GPA and 29 ACT, $2,500) and MTAG (2.5 GPA and 15 ACT; $500 to $1,000; due September 15). Students get only one of these state grants a term (the larger one), for up to 8 semesters, and need 12 credit hours a term. Superscored ACTs are accepted. The state warned that spring 2027 awards could be cut if the budget gap isn't closed.
